memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then God said, "Yes, but your wife Sarah will bear you a son, and you will call him Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him." - Gen 17:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's answer begins with a beautiful word: "Yes." Yes, He hears Abraham's prayer for Ishmael (as the next verse shows). "But" - God also holds firmly to His own plan: the covenant would come through Isaac, the son not yet born. God honours Abraham's heart while keeping His purpose. His "yes" to our prayers and His "no" to our preferred plan are not contradictions.

Notice that God even names the coming son: Isaac, "he laughs." The laughter of Abraham's astonishment becomes the name of the child of promise. What began as staggered disbelief God transforms into a name that would forever declare joy. God takes our wavering wonder and makes something beautiful of it.

There is comfort here in how God handles our prayers. He does not always give us exactly what we ask in the way we ask it. But He is never dismissive of our requests, and His own plan is always better than the one we would have chosen. Abraham wanted blessing through Ishmael; God had something greater in Isaac.

We can trust a God like this. He listens to our hearts and holds to His wisdom. Sometimes His answer is "yes, and also something better than you asked." Isaac would be the child through whom, generations later, the Messiah Himself would come (Matt 1:2). God's plan is always worth trusting above our own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Can you trust God's plan even when it differs from your request?
- How has God given you something better than what you asked for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You hear my prayers and yet hold to Your wiser plan. Help me trust that Your purposes are always better than mine, and that Your answers, even when unexpected, are good.
Amen.
